approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Climate Trigger) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create a new climate trigger under the EPBC Act for assessing greenhouse gas emissions from projects.

It would set two emission thresholds: a significant impact level for emissions between 25,000 and 100,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per year, requiring ministerial consideration, and a prohibited impact level above 100,000 tonnes, forcing the minister to reject approval.
The bill would also require the Climate Change Authority to produce a national carbon budget to 2050 and update it annually, against which the minister must assess projects.
Establishes a new class of controlled action for greenhouse gas emissions.
Creates two emission thresholds—25,000 to 100,000 tonnes (significant impact) and above 100,000 tonnes (prohibited impact).
Requires the Climate Change Authority to develop and annually update a national carbon budget to 2050.
Bans the minister from using alternative approval processes for actions with a significant impact on emissions, except for limited exceptions.
Proponents of emissions-intensive projects and the Minister for the Environment would be affected.
